pdf_license: publisher-paywall (Elsevier, Clinical Neurophysiology); specification page carries no licence statement
notes: Two documents exist for this standard and neither could be archived. The journal article, Kemp and Olivan (2003), Clinical Neurophysiology 114(9):1755-1761, doi confirmed against Crossref, is paywalled -- Unpaywall reports is_oa false with zero oa_locations as of 2026-07-31 -- and was not retrieved. The canonical specification at https://www.edfplus.info/specs/edfplus.html is publicly readable but carries NO licence statement of any kind: no copyright line, no terms of use, no public-domain declaration. Because a licence that cannot be positively identified is unknown rather than permissive, no copy is committed. pdf_status is not-redistributable rather than not-applicable because a paper does exist; source.md is a plain-text snapshot of the specification page, retained as internal research notes, with a header recording that provenance. md_quality is partial, and the reason is specific and load-bearing: the specification's annotation mechanism is defined in terms of the unprintable delimiter bytes 20 (0x14) and 21 (0x15), and the HTML-to-text conversion silently dropped them, so every worked Time-stamped Annotations List example lost its field boundaries and several definitional sentences are ungrammatical as extracted. The byte layout recorded on the card was reconstructed from the surrounding prose, which names the byte values explicitly, and should be checked against the live page before implementation. Also damaged: 57 lines of shredded tables including the section 3.7 header-record table, which survives as an alternating stream of field and value fragments; the section 3.3 sleep-scoring example, which was read column-wise and is now out of chronological order and must not be read as a sequence; five non-ASCII characters lost to replacement characters in the acknowledgement names; and a linked logarithmic-transformation formula that is absent entirely. The conversion also inserted a blank line between every wrapped line, so the file is 1968 lines for 33 KB.
